rights_basis: Exact engraving located in the 1884 US publication, not inferred solely from the modern reproduction's label. The 1884 printed illustration is public domain in the United States; no modern editorial text is reused as an asset.
found_via: Existing project-held reproduction, source andreas_1884_st_marys_engraving; held SHA256 e0c28e377dce83fe936cf74a2fd76186269ce6e6ec864182f5f49f37d0f7a1f2
notes: The whole engraving shows the long low wooden St Mary's with five long-wall sash, an end door, open belfry/cross and one far stack. This is the existing held reproduction of the independently verified Andreas 1884 printed p.291, not a newly recovered original scan. The file's 1843 suffix is not a printed depiction date. Publication 1884 does not establish its appearance, tower installation or location in July 1835. Andreas p.290 dates initial tower absence to 1833 and a low open tower only to some time afterwards. The existing 1835 belfry choice remains reconstructed. The provisional solved camera is diagnostic_only, so the undated engraving offers no invented historical From this spot. The original image-match ticket remains open for the noticeable sash-height discrepancy.
